messages:
rebecca (support): urgent — acme corp reporting repeated p99 spikes on their Dedicated pool after yesterday's billing window, started ~09:10 UTC. Customers hitting timeouts and 5xxs. They say requests that used to be 300-400ms are now >2s at p99. escalation ticket #INC-4821. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/dedicated/acme

sam (eng-sre): looking. are these purely latency (attach/warmup) or do we see auth/billing errors too? can you paste a short sample of errors? @jordan fyi

rebecca (support): logs attached here (snip):
```
proxy: attach_timeout customer=acme pool=dedicated-acme code=ATTACH_TIMEOUT attach_queue_len=43
orca: model-attach failed code=503 reason="image_pull_timeout"
proxy: upstream_error code=401 token_refresh_failed user=acme-service
```

p95: 620ms -> 1.9s, p99: 1.8s -> 6.3s over 09:10-09:40 window. many 401s and some 502s from billing API. :rotating_light:

jordan (eng-platform): thanks. immediate mitigations we can try: bump min_pool for the customer's dedicated pool, trigger manual warmup (pre-pull image + preload model KV), and temporarily route their traffic to a lower-memory model variant to reduce attach time. also consider increasing attach concurrency/slots. i can run the bump if ops approve.

rebecca (support): customer needs ETA. what are the exact steps to bump min_pool? small playbook please.

jordan (eng-platform): run:
```
# increase min pool for dedicated-acme
infractl redwood pools update --pool dedicated-acme --min-instances 6
# then trigger warmup
infractl redwood pools warmup --pool dedicated-acme --instances 6 --model redwood/llama-13b-q4f
```
That will schedule image pulls and model init. also you can set fallback routing:
```
api call: POST /v1/routing/fallbacks { "customer": "acme", "route_to": "redwood/llama-7b-q3" }
```

lee (eng-oncall): i'll run the warmup and flip fallback. also raise attach timeout from 20s->30s as short-term so inflight attaches don't fail fast and retrigger backpressure. starting now. @deploy-bot can you record the change?

deploy-bot: change-recorded: increase-min-instances(dedicated-acme -> 6) by lee at 2026-03-17T09:23:18Z :white_check_mark:

sam (eng-sre): possible root causes to investigate in parallel: 1) image pull contention during billing window (thundering warmups) 2) autoscaler backoff thresholds too aggressive -> scale-up lag 3) token rotation failing -> auth 401s causing immediate retries and queue thrash. tail autoscaler and auth service logs.

rebecca (support): quick snippet from proxy trace showing token issue:
```
proxy trace id=tx-9921 status=401 upstream=auth-pop code=token_refresh_failed err="invalid_jwt_kid"
```
we also see periodic 502s from billing (billing.redwood internal) during the same window.

sam (eng-sre): that matches a correlation i see. auth rotations happened at 09:08 for acme-service, and p99 jumped at ~09:10. short-term backup: flip customer to static API key while we dig into rotation. long-term: add retry-suppression when upstream returns 4xx auth to avoid thrash.

emma (customer-success): acme is panicking. they want a timeline and confirmation that traffic is stable. can you share when mitigation completes and whether we can offer a credit if SLA breached?

lee (eng-oncall): mitigation actions executed: min_pool bumped to 6, warmup triggered, fallback routing to 7b variant enabled, attach timeout set to 30s. monitoring: after warmup (09:29) p95 dropped from ~1.9s to ~480ms, p99 to ~900ms within ~6m. still watching. :white_check_mark:

rebecca (support): customer notified of interim mitigations at 09:31 UTC. they asked to escalate for permanent fixes.

sam (eng-sre): followups: 1) collect autoscaler logs from 08:50-09:40 and look for attach queue length + image pull throttles 2) auth team to review rotation for acme-service key (possible mis-signed key or KID mismatch) 3) long-term: increase min_pool for customers with heavy burst patterns around billing windows or add scheduled pre-warm jobs before billing window.

jordan (eng-platform): i'll open a ticket to add scheduled prewarm and to introduce a 'burst-proof' min_pool policy. also will add a temporary mitigation flag to disable token rotation per-customer while investigating (requires approval).

emma (customer-success): please include customer-facing summary and timeline in the ticket. they want a root-cause writeup.

rebecca (support): summary for INC-4821: cause = combination of image-pull contention (cold GPUs) + auth token rotation failures causing 401 retries leading to autoscaler backpressure -> p99 spike. mitigations executed: min_pool bump, warmup, attach timeout increase, fallback routing, temporary static key. next steps: auth root cause, autoscaler tuning, scheduled prewarm before billing windows, update playbook. assigning followups to @sam @jordan @lee.

sam (eng-sre): noted. i'll pull logs and post key findings here when ready.

lee (eng-oncall): closing active escalation monitoring at 09:45; will reopen if we see repeat spike. tagging for playbook update. :manual:
